summary: Clock skew between control-plane replicas causes canary evaluator to misclassify cohort; tenant traffic diverted to quantized fallback with quality drop
description:
Issue summary:
Control-plane replicas in us-east-1 had up to ~6s of clock skew after a maintenance window. The canary evaluator includes a timestamped snapshot comparison step that uses monotonic timestamps to bind snapshots to rollout epochs. Because two evaluator replicas disagreed on the epoch boundary, the cohort evaluator incorrectly marked a small subset (~0.6% of BrightHealth AI tenant traffic) as failing the canary health check. Routing policy triggered automatic fallback to the quantized variant (redwood/gpt-small-quantized-v2) for affected sessions, bypassing the pinned model selection for those sessions.

Impact:
- BrightHealth AI reported degraded output quality (semantic incompleteness and tokenization artifacts) for a subset of production requests between 2026-03-12T03:07Z and 2026-03-12T03:23Z.
- Estimated affected traffic: 0.6% of tenant traffic; error budget impact minimal but customer-visible quality regression.
- No increase in 5xx errors or latency spikes observed; issue is functional (quality) and routing-related.

Environment:
- Platform: Redwood Hosted API (prod).
- Region: us-east-1.
- Targeted tenant: BrightHealth AI (enterprise account with a model pin to redwood/gpt-small-8bit-v2).

Steps to reproduce (observed path):
1) Canary rollout initiated for a different tenant in us-east-1; canary evaluator takes a timestamped snapshot (epoch T).
2) Control-plane replica A has NTP sync drift +6s relative to replica B after maintenance; evaluator on A uses epoch T+1 boundary while B uses T.
3) Evaluator snapshot fingerprint mismatch triggers canary failure for the cohort that crosses the boundary.
4) Routing policy (canary_auto_fallback=true, pin_preservation=false for this minor cohort) routes the affected sessions to the quantized fallback variant.
5) Customer traffic experiences quality regression for the duration of the misclassification window.

Observed behavior:
- Canary evaluator logs show ‘epoch_mismatch’ events stamped with discordant timestamps.
- Orchestrator trace shows cohort_hash -> fallback_variant for affected request IDs.
- Serving logs for quantized model show normal throughput and latency.
- No authorization or quota errors in customer logs.

Expected behavior:
- Canary evaluator should only mark a cohort as failing if both replicas consistently report failure for the same epoch.
- Tenant-level model pin should be honored (pin_preservation=true) or at minimum, fallback must preserve pin preference for enterprise-tier tenants unless explicit override is configured.

Attachments / logs:
- Excerpts from canary-evaluator logs (lines with epoch_mismatch) attached to ticket.
- Short trace from orchestrator (trace IDs: trace-1a2b3c, trace-4d5e6f).
- Customer-provided examples of degraded outputs (redacted) included.
comments: 2026-03-12 04:12 - Aisha Kapoor (Support): Customer BrightHealth AI reported clinical-case summarization outputs missing sections. They provided 12 example request IDs. Marking as high priority due to enterprise tier.

2026-03-12 04:27 - Diego Morales (Oncall Eng): Observed epoch_mismatch events in canary-evaluator in us-east-1. Opened INT-1034 to investigate control-plane time drift. Temporarily set canary_auto_fallback=false for affected rollout slices to prevent further automatic diversion.

2026-03-12 05:05 - SRE Team (comment): NTP service on two control-plane replicas delayed sync during post-maintenance; offset measured ~+5.8s. Forced NTP resync and reloaded evaluator service. Re-running canary evaluation; no failures reproducing after resync.

2026-03-12 05:42 - Diego Morales (Oncall Eng): Rolled canary_auto_fallback back to true with safer pin_preservation override for enterprise tenants. Notified CS to inform customer of mitigation and next steps.
2026-03-12 08:10 - CS Rep (Marta Ruiz): Reached out to BrightHealth AI with incident summary and apology. Customer acknowledged and requested postmortem and assurance to prevent recurrence.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: evaluator algorithm bug incorrectly tolerates single-replica disagreement -> confirmed mismatch due to timestamp discordance rather than algorithmic logic error.

Control-plane replicas had NTP jitter after maintenance; canary evaluator uses wall-clock to compute epoch boundaries. We observed two distinct epoch boundaries within a short window -> led to split decision.
Routing policy configured with pin_preservation=false for minor cohorts to allow rapid fallbacks; this combined with evaluator split to divert pinned sessions unexpectedly.
No kernel/serving-runtime performance issue detected; quality regression traced to model variant difference (8bit vs quantized tokenization mapping).
resolution: Mitigation applied 2026-03-12 05:10Z: forced NTP resync on affected control-plane replicas and restarted canary-evaluator to clear mismatched snapshots.
Short-term policy change: set pin_preservation=true for all enterprise-tier tenants and blocked automatic fallback on pinned routes while root cause investigation proceeds.
Customer remediation: support rolled back affected requests by replaying with the pinned model for the provided example request IDs; customer validated outputs as acceptable.

Ticketed follow-up to engineering (INT-1034) for durable fix in canary evaluator: move to epoch-consensus protocol rather than single-replica wall-clock boundary and add monitoring for control-plane time drift.
Status: In Progress - engineering PR for evaluator consensus in review (see related_github_prs).
follow_up_actions: ENG: Implement epoch-consensus change in canary-evaluator and add tolerant comparison that requires majority agreement across control-plane replicas before triggering fallback (linked INT-1034).
SRE: Harden NTP monitoring and alerting for control-plane fleet; add automated resync playbook in Confluence.
PLATFORM: Change default routing policy to preserve tenant pins for dedicated/enterprise tiers and make pin_preservation opt-out rather than opt-in.
CS/Account: Prepare customer-facing postmortem and share within 3 business days.
